title: Long exact sequence for cohomology with support
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $F$ be a
torsion etale sheaf on the
small etale site of $X$. In the
notation of [def-pur-support-cohomology], there is a long exact
sequence

$$
\cdots\longrightarrow H^q_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,F)
\longrightarrow H^q(U,F)\longrightarrow H^{q+1}_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow\cdots,
$$

functorial in the pair $(X,X\setminus Z)$ and in $F$. The same
statement holds for bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology in the
derived category of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and on the
pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of $X$ for finite-torsion coefficients.
(Source: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 9, Theorem 9.4;
the bounded-below and pro-etale extensions follow from the site argument below.)

external.place: (Source: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 9, Theorem 9.3 and the exactness axiom of the etale site.) Step 1: the derived support object.

proof.text: Work on a small site $\mathcal C$ with terminal object $T$ and a monomorphism $V\to T$; eventually these are $X$ and its open subscheme $U$; the inclusion is a monomorphism since two morphisms into the open subscheme whose composites into $X$ agree have identical underlying maps and identical maps on the restricted structure sheaves. We use abelian sheaves, not the subcategory of torsion sheaves, to take resolutions. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] this abelian category has enough injectives. For any cohomologically bounded-below object $K$, choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^r(K)=0$ for $r<a$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose a complex $I$ of injective abelian sheaves with $I^r=0$ for $r<a$ and an isomorphism $QI\simeq K$. In particular $I$ is K-injective. For a torsion sheaf take $K=F[0]$ and choose $a=0$, so that $I$ and all three section complexes below vanish in negative degrees. No assertion that every K-injective complex is termwise injective is needed.

source.place: Tag 013K (injective resolutions exist), bounded-below injective resolution construction and Tag 070J (bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective)

proof.text: Set $S(G)=\ker(G(T)\to G(V))$. On the scheme sites this is exactly the group-valued kernel-of-restriction functor $\Gamma_Z(X,G)$ in the current statement of [def-pur-support-cohomology], on all abelian sheaves. That definition also specifies its bounded-below right derived functor and, separately, the identical construction on the pro-etale site; no site-comparison identification is part of this definition. Evaluation is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus $S$ is additive and left exact: a section in the kernel of a sheaf map is a section of its kernel, and being zero after restriction is the same condition in that subsheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to the three additive functors $S$, $G\mapsto G(T)$ and $G\mapsto G(V)$. Their derived values on $K$ are represented respectively by $S(I)$, $I(T)$ and $I(V)$. For $F[0]$ this agrees with the ordinary right-derived-functor definition in [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

source.place: Section 9, pp. 65-67, definition of sections with support and Theorem 9.4; derived-complex computation: Stacks Tags 05TI and 05TH

proof.text:
The monomorphism $V\to T$ and injectivity of each $I^r$ satisfy precisely the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction]. Therefore $I^r(T)\to I^r(V)$ is surjective in every degree. Its kernel is $S(I^r)$ by construction. Restriction commutes with the differential, so these degreewise sequences form a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow S(I)\longrightarrow I(T)\longrightarrow I(V)\longrightarrow0.$$
This proves surjectivity only for the terms of the injective resolution, not for the original sheaf.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective; specialize the ring to the constant integers

proof.text: To identify the last complex on a scheme, localize at the object $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives], restriction to $\mathcal C/V$ is exact, and by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] it preserves injective abelian sheaves. Hence $I|_V$ is a bounded-below injective complex representing $K|_V$. The equality of complexes $I(V)=\Gamma(\mathrm{id}_V,I|_V)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identify its cohomology with $H^q(\mathcal C/V,K|_V)$ in all integer degrees. In the etale case [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-over-open] identifies the localized site with $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and its restriction with $j^{-1}$, so this is $H^q(U,j^{-1}K)$. These statements require neither quasi-compactness of $U$ nor a Noetherian hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open, including its exact-extension-by-zero proof; the etale slice identification is the cited node

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] in the abelian category of abelian groups to the degreewise short exact sequence in Step 3. Using Steps 2 and 4 gives
$$\cdots\to H^q_Z(X,K)\to H^q(X,K)\to H^q(U,j^{-1}K)\xrightarrow{\delta^q}H^{q+1}_Z(X,K)\to\cdots.$$
The first two arrows are induced by inclusion of the kernel and restriction. For $K=F[0]$ the complexes vanish in negative degrees, so the usual sequence begins with $0\to H^0_Z(X,F)\to H^0(X,F)$. For general bounded-below $K$ the same construction works in every integer degree; its injective terms need not have torsion, since the torsion hypothesis concerns cohomology of $K$.

For a morphism $a:K\to K'$ on the same site, choose bounded-below injective representatives $I,I'$. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a chain map $h:I\to I'$ representing $a$, unique up to chain homotopy. Naturality of restriction gives a commuting square $I(T)\to I(V)$ over $I'(T)\to I'(V)$, and the map on kernels is $S(h)$. Thus this is a morphism of the short exact sequences of Step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], the cohomology maps commute with every $\delta^q$. Additive evaluation and $S$ send a chain homotopy to a chain homotopy (apply the functor to $h-h'=ds+sd$); hence the cohomology maps depend only on $a$. Changing the injective representative gives the same identification, since a comparison quasi-isomorphism of K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence by the same Hom-derived lemma. This establishes coefficient functoriality and independence of choices, including the boundary maps.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; boundary naturality: Stacks homology.tex Tag 0117

proof.text:
Here is the map for pairs, including its compatibility with the boundary. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a morphism, let $U'\subset X'$ be open with $U'\subset f^{-1}U$, and let $Z'$ be a closed subscheme with complement $U'$. Equivalently, the underlying closed subsets satisfy $f^{-1}(|Z|)\subset |Z'|$; taking complements gives exactly the open inclusion needed below. This includes the inverse-image pair $U'=f^{-1}U$. Given $a:f^{-1}K\to L$, choose bounded-below injective representatives $I$ of $K$ and $J$ of $L$. The inverse/direct-image adjunctions and sectionwise direct-image formulas are [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] in the etale case and [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] in the pro-etale case. For arbitrary morphisms of schemes, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] says directly that etale inverse image is additive and exact. On the pro-etale site, [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] constructs the morphism of sites, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] applies. Hence in either case $f^{-1}I$ represents $f^{-1}K$. Since $J$ is K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $a$ by a chain map $f^{-1}I\to J$, unique up to homotopy. Its adjoint $b:I\to f_*J$ gives the two chain maps
$$I(X)\to J(X'),\qquad I(U)\to J(f^{-1}U)\to J(U').$$
Their square with restriction commutes because $b$ is a morphism of sheaves and $U'\subset f^{-1}U$. Consequently the first map sends $\ker(I(X)\to I(U))$ into $\ker(J(X')\to J(U'))$. These three maps form a morphism of the short exact complexes in Step 3, so [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] makes all squares, including the connecting squares, commute. If $h-h'=ds+sd$ for the two chosen coefficient chain maps, transpose its components to degree $-1$ maps $t^r:I^r\to f_*J^{r-1}$. Naturality of $t$ with respect to restriction shows that $t_X$ sends a section vanishing on $U$ to one vanishing on $U'$. Therefore $t$ gives a homotopy on the support kernels as well as on global and open sections. All three induced cohomology maps are independent of the choice of chain map. Use [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] for the etale site and [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] for the pro-etale site to identify successive inverse images with the inverse image of the composite, compatibly with the adjunction units and the canonical fibre-product identifications of direct images. For identities take the identity chain map. For a second pair map $g:X''\to X'$ with $U''\subset g^{-1}U'$, choose an injective representative $P$ on $X''$ and coefficient chain maps $h:f^{-1}I\to J$ and $k:g^{-1}J\to P$. Under $(f\circ g)^{-1}I\cong g^{-1}f^{-1}I$, the chain map for the composite is $k\circ g^{-1}h$. The unit compatibility in the cited composition theorem identifies its adjoint with $I\to f_*J\to f_*g_*P$. On global sections this adjoint evaluates to $I(X)\to J(X')\to P(X'')$. On open sections, naturality of $J\to g_*P$ for $U'\subset f^{-1}U$ shows that $I(U)\to J(f^{-1}U)\to P(g^{-1}f^{-1}U)\to P(U'')$ equals $I(U)\to J(U')\to P(g^{-1}U')\to P(U'')$, since $U''\subset g^{-1}U'$. Thus both section maps equal the previously defined composites. Restricting those equal maps to the support kernels gives equality there too. Uniqueness up to the homotopies just described proves the composition law for any choices of representative maps. This proves the asserted functoriality in pairs and in coefficients, rather than assuming a base-change isomorphism.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4 (functoriality); explicit chain-map construction from exact site inverse image (Stacks Tag 00YV) and K-injective Hom comparison (Tag 070I)

proof.text: Finally take the small pro-etale site of the arbitrary scheme $X$, with the size conventions in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The theorem [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] explicitly includes open immersions and identifies $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, including their coverings and constant coefficient sheaves; it also states that an open immersion is a monomorphism. Restriction preserves injectives and derived evaluation agrees with derived sections on $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] (use the constant integers for abelian sheaves). Explicitly, for a bounded-below pro-etale complex $K$ with the finite-torsion coefficients of [def-pur-support-cohomology], choose its termwise-injective abelian-sheaf representative $I$ as in Step 1. The three complexes of Steps 2-3 are $\ker(I(X)\to I(U))$, $I(X)$ and $I(U)$ on this site. Their sequence is short exact in every degree by Step 3, since $U\to X$ is monic. Their cohomology groups are respectively $H^q_Z(X,K)$, $H^q(X,K)$ and $H^q(U,j^{-1}K)$: the first identification is the cited support definition and Step 2, and the last follows from the cited exact, injective-preserving localization and Step 4. Step 5 therefore supplies the displayed long exact sequence. For a coefficient map the morphism of these three complexes is $(S(h),h_X,h_U)$ from Step 6. For a pair map $f:X'\to X$ with $U'\subset f^{-1}U$, it is the restriction to the support kernel of $b_X:I(X)\to J(X')$, together with $b_X$ and $I(U)\to J(f^{-1}U)\to J(U')$, where $b$ is the pro-etale adjoint chain map constructed in Step 7. The restriction square commutes, so Step 7 gives boundary compatibility, independence of choices and the identity and composition laws for these maps. This is a direct site argument for all such pro-etale sheaves or bounded-below complexes, whether or not they descend from the etale site. In particular no Noetherian, constructibility, or quasi-compact-complement condition has been introduced.

split_report.summary: Eight proof steps construct the degreewise short exact sequence of supported sections, global sections and open sections on a bounded-below termwise-injective resolution, identify the derived terms, and prove coefficient and pair functoriality by explicit chain maps. The same arbitrary-site argument proves the finite-torsion pro-etale clause. No new nodes. Corrected the imported arbitrary-sheaf surjectivity error, the claim that K-injective implies termwise injective, the unsupported use of comparison for all pro-etale coefficients, and the Milne theorem number. No mathematical hypothesis or conclusion was weakened. Fresh stage-1 rereading removed an inherited sandbox-only partial Lean record, applied the previously reported citation/explanation correction to the actual statement, and added the pro-etale site definition as a statement dependency. Stage-2 H1/H2 are outside this assignment and are not stage-1 blockers. Repair of the merge-lock return: reread every current statement dependency and proof citation, checked all 27 quotations, clarified use of the expanded support definition in Step 2 and the pair-map condition in Step 7, and rebuilt the stage-1 delivery on current origin through deliver.py --no-push. No new nodes or dependency edges.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-3 realize blueprint Steps 1-2 (derived sections and exactness), repairing false surjectivity for arbitrary sheaves; Steps 4-7 realize its Step 3 including all naturality; Step 8 realizes Step 4 directly on the pro-etale site, because full faithfulness alone does not prove a statement for objects outside the etale essential image. This preserves the unit route: the support long exact sequence is the input for its affine-line/open-complement argument.

lean.note: Canonical derived inclusion and restriction; natural connecting maps on bounded-below torsion etale coefficients and finite-level pro-etale coefficients. Pair functoriality is expressed on every injective representative, using the actual adjoint chain map and base-change restriction, and the unique induced map on the support kernels. Degree-zero single objects recover the ordinary sheaf sequence via the existing canonical comparison of bounded-below and classical right derived functors.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $F$ be a
torsion etale sheaf on the
small etale site of $X$. In the
notation of [def-pur-support-cohomology], there is a long exact
sequence

$$
\cdots\longrightarrow H^q_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,F)
\longrightarrow H^q(U,F)\longrightarrow H^{q+1}_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow\cdots,
$$

functorial in the pair $(X,X\setminus Z)$ and in $F$. The same
statement holds for bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology in the
derived category of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and on the
pro-etale site of $X$ for finite-torsion coefficients, by the comparison
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison].

proof.text:
Step 1: the derived support object. For a bounded-below complex $F$ (a torsion sheaf placed in degree zero) and
$I^{\bullet}$ a K-injective resolution, the complex of sections with
support in $Z$ is the kernel of the restriction
$\Gamma(X,I^{\bullet})\to\Gamma(U,I^{\bullet})$, which is exact, and the
kernel is the complex computing $R\Gamma_Z(X,\cdot)$ by
[def-pur-support-cohomology]. Step 2: the exactness axiom. For a
torsion sheaf $F$ the sequence of presheaves
$0\to\Gamma_Z(V,F)\to\Gamma(V,F)\to\Gamma(V\cap U,F)\to0$ is exact for
every open $V$ of the finite-type scheme $X$: a section $f$ of
$F$ on $V\cap U$ need not extend, but for the sheaf $F$ the exact
sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to i_*i^*F\to0$ is exact (the open and
closed counterpart of the recollement, the standard exactness of
support and restriction on the (pro-)etale site,
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement]) and its global-sections
sequence is the sequence of the statement. Step 3: the long exact
sequence. The short exact sequence of complexes

$$
0\longrightarrow\Gamma_Z(X,I^{\bullet})
\longrightarrow\Gamma(X,I^{\bullet})
\longrightarrow\Gamma(U,I^{\bullet})\longrightarrow0
$$

(the exactness at the last arrow holding because $I^{\bullet}$ is
K-injective, hence flabby on the (pro-)etale site: the restriction map
of a flabby resolution is surjective, by Step 2 applied to an
injective resolution and the flabbiness of injective sheaves on a
site) gives, by the zig-zag/snake lemma applied to the exact sequence
of cochain complexes, the long exact sequence of cohomology

$$
\cdots\to H^q_Z(X,F)\to H^q(X,F)\to H^q(U,F)\to H^{q+1}_Z(X,F)\to\cdots,
$$

with the connecting morphism the one of the K-injective
resolution; the functoriality in the pair and in $F$ is the
functoriality of all the maps. Step 4: complexes and the pro-etale
site. For bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology the same
argument runs with a K-injective resolution (the exactness of the
level (2) sequence for each term and the five-lemma over the
spectral sequence of the double complex), and the finite-torsion case
on the pro-etale site is the transport of the etale statement along
the site comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] of the proper-base-change chapter (the sheaves being finite-torsion, the site comparison preserves
the support and the exactness).
